$comment: EXP-1291 Team settings → Agents ×4, managed exactly like boards. MCP (#FEED-195): `exponential_agents` writes through the same `agents` router as this page, so its rules are this page's: `create` {teamId, name, deviceId, instructions?, triggers?, skillIds?, mcpServerIds?, icon?, color?, cli?, account?, model?}, `update` {id, any of those but teamId} and `delete` {id} are for the team's owners (a member's Assistant is theirs alone: its triggers and device stay editable, its prompt is fixed, it is never deleted, and nothing creates one here). A confined MCP grant needs the agent's team. Triggers are written whole (`triggers` replaces the list; keep a trigger's `id` from `get` to keep its firing history), each {kind: schedule, cron, tz?} or {kind: event, name}, `enabled: false` switches one off; there is no per-agent switch. Replies never carry `triggerState`. The list = Settings rows (icon + color + name like a board row, then `New agent`); an agent page = the board page layout, `fields` top to bottom: identity (the board form's ONE field: icon picker + color swatch + name), Device (required; the device picker, online devices of the team the caller may start on), Account (the device's account picker, optional = the device's last used login; EXP-1306: the row's VALUE reads exactly like the composer's account picker chip = the picked login's agent brand mark + its email (`options` = the logins the device reports, `accountName` ladder; the agent-named stand-in row a profile-less device gets in the composer never counts), never the agent's name alone and never dimmed while editable; `agentAccountValue({options, account, cli})` replays `accountValueCases`: the option whose id == the pinned `account` (and whose agent == `cli` when set), else `cli`'s first option, else the last used option (isLastUsed), else the first; none = null and the row reads `copy.accountLastUsed` muted), Triggers (NEW-2: one row per trigger reading `triggerSummary`, a toggle per row, `+ Add` opens the trigger editor: a schedule = THE schedule picker (`schedule-picker.json`: Repeat · Days/Day · Time · Time zone rows; the stored form is a 5-field cron in an IANA zone, #N-2, never typed), an event = the name of an `events` row (the builtins `contract.events.builtinNames` or any custom name); none = the agent only waits for messages), Instructions (markdown, server-only: `sessions.getAgent`, placeholder `copy.instructionsPlaceholder`), Delete (owner-only, confirms with `copy.deleteConfirm`). Owner-only controls are hidden from members (they read). Save = `agents.create` for a new agent, `agents.update` after (NEW-2: an agent is a definition row; its conversations follow it). triggerSummary(trigger) (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/agent-settings.ts; mirrors desktop domain::agent_settings, iOS AgentSettings.swift, Android AgentSettings.kt) replays `summaryCases`: schedule = `scheduleSummary(cron, tz)` of `schedule-picker.json` (`Every day at 09:00 (Europe/Vienna)`; a cron the rows cannot express reads `Cron …`); event = `copy.events[name]` for a builtin name, else `copy.event` with {name}; a disabled trigger appends ' · Paused'. validateAgentForm(form) replays `validationCases`: errors keyed by field, in field order: name blank (after trim) → copy.errors.nameRequired, over agentNameMax (contract sessionsSend) → copy.errors.nameTooLong, no device → copy.errors.deviceRequired, instructions over agentInstructionsMaxBytes UTF-8 bytes → copy.errors.instructionsTooLong; [] = valid. #EXP-1850 (owner 2026-11-14, #EXP-1829 plan): THE trigger list lists EVERY kind ×4: `triggerSummary` reads a record trigger as `copy.record` ({record} = its kind, {op} = `copy.recordOps`) and a webhook as `copy.webhook`; a trigger carrying `run` gets a SECOND line `triggerDetail` = `copy.runs` with `runLabel(run)` (`records.<op> <kind>`, the action name, `<upstream>/<tool>`) or `copy.handsOff` for an `{agent}` run, null otherwise (`detailCases`). The editor (`+ Add`, a row's tap, ⋯ Edit) edits a schedule or an event; a record or webhook row has no editor (⋯ = Delete only); an edit keeps every other key of the stored trigger (prompt, run, preset). Every write sends `triggerKinds` = all four kinds (agents.update: the kinds a writer names are replaced, the rest kept).

page.$comment: #EXP-1846 (owner 2026-11-14, #EXP-1835 plan option B): ONE AGENT PAGE ×4 for the Assistant AND every team agent, SUPERSEDING `fields` order and `assistant.sections`. `sections` top to bottom, each a header (`copy[label]`) over one grouped card: `identity` (the board form's icon picker + colour swatch + name; the Assistant: its brand mark + name, never icon/colour), `runs-on` (rows in order: device, account, model, skills, mcp-servers; #EXP-1988: the Assistant's page draws no skills / mcp-servers row here but one section per team of its member right after `runs-on` (`team-picks`, `assistant.teamPicks`); the MODEL row is every agent's now, value = `assistantModelValue({model, cli})` for any agent; mcp-servers keeps `mcpRow`'s visibility; the Assistant's device picker keeps NEW-99's desktops-only list, a team agent lists every team device), `triggers` (header `copy.triggers` with the `+ Add` pill on its trailing edge for editors; first row = `check-in`: THE single-select Picker in its row trigger over `assistant.schedules` (Off · Every 15 minutes · Every 30 minutes · Every hour · Every day), value `checkInOf(triggers)`; a pick writes `withCheckIn(triggers, id, tz)` whole; then one row per `listedTriggers(triggers)` (triggerSummary · Switch · ⋯ Edit/Delete, the row opens the editor); a PAUSED trigger's row = its sentence WITHOUT the ` · Paused` suffix in the muted text colour, the switch off: the same row ×4; no empty-state row (Check in `Off` says it); `+ Add` opens THE trigger editor (schedule or event), for the Assistant too), `voice` (#EXP-1847: every agent, `voice` below; the Assistant adds its member rows), `instructions` (team agents only; the Assistant's prompt is built in), `delete` (team agents only, owners). EDITORS: a team agent's rows are its team's OWNERS' (members read every row, no `+ Add`, no ⋯, no Delete); the Assistant's are its member's. THE TRIGGER LIST is ONE reusable piece per platform taking an agent id (web AgentTriggers, desktop settings::agent_triggers, iOS AgentTriggersSection, Android AgentTriggersSection) so the app screen's Events tab (#EXP-1829) mounts the same rows.

checkIn.$comment: #EXP-1846: THE CHECK IN = the ONE schedule trigger carrying `preset` (an `assistant.schedules` id other than `off`; its `cron` is that preset's cron, the server refuses a mismatch and a second preset). It lives in `agents.triggers` beside the other triggers and fires exactly like them (wakeups.json); only the page shows it apart. `checkInOf(triggers)` (`checkInCases`) = the preset trigger's id, `off` when there is none or it is paused (enabled false). `withCheckIn(triggers, id, tz)` (`withCheckInCases`) = the triggers with the preset trigger replaced IN FRONT (it keeps its `id`, and so its firing history, and its stored `tz`; a new one takes `tz` when given) or removed for `off`; every other trigger stays as it is, in order. `listedTriggers(triggers)` (`listedCases`) = every trigger WITHOUT `preset`, in order (the rows under Check in). Any agent may hold one; the Assistant may now hold other schedule and event triggers too (`agents.update` no longer refuses them: `assistant.copy.scheduleRefused` is kept for old clients only). MIGRATION 0282 tagged each Assistant's single preset-cron schedule with its preset. An OLD client's Assistant page still writes one untagged preset schedule: the server tags an Assistant's write that is exactly one untagged schedule on a preset cron (`legacyCheckIn`).

voice.$comment: #EXP-1847 phase a (owner 2026-11-14, plan approved: fall back to the member's voice device; the clip is UPLOADED as the agent's file; phases a→b→c→d). EVERY agent's page gets the `voice` section (agent-settings.json `page`, no longer Assistant-only): rows in order `rows` under header `copy.label`, the same Picker/input rows ×4. DATA: `agents.voice` (SYNCED jsonb, `{}` = the member's): `language` (etalk voice.json `languages`), `clipId` + `clipName` (an `attachments` row uploaded through POST `clipUpload.route` (multipart part `file`, `clipUpload.accept`, at most `clipUpload.maxBytes`; answers {clipId, clipName}; DELETE clears it), never swept while an agent names it), `transcript` (at most `limits.transcript`), `wakePhrase` (at most `limits.wakePhrase`; a non-empty phrase needs `limits.wakePhraseMinLetters` letters, voice.json `wakePhraseError`). Written with `agents.update {voice: {language?, transcript?, wakePhrase?}}` (a key set to null clears it); the clip only through the route. Editors as `page`: a team agent's owners, the Assistant's member. ROWS: `language` = THE single-select Picker row over voice.json `languages`, value = `agentVoiceOf(...).language`; `clip` = the row's value `agentVoiceOf(...).clipLabel` (`copy.clipBuiltIn` when none, in the row's usual value colour), a press opens the platform's file picker (accept `clipUpload.accept`) and uploads; a set clip offers `copy.clipRemove` (the row's ⋯ / trailing action); failures toast (`copy.errors`); `transcript` and `wakePhrase` = THE input rows (placeholder `copy.transcriptPlaceholder` / `copy.wakePhrasePlaceholder` with {agent} = the agent's name), saved on blur/enter, the wake phrase's error inline. THE ASSISTANT: these four rows REPLACE voice.json's Language / Voice file / Transcript / Wake phrase rows on its page; its member rows (push to talk, wake word on/off, meetings) stay below them, unchanged. RESOLUTION `agentVoiceOf({role, name, voice}, member)` (`voiceOfCases`; member = the member's voice.get settings): language = voice.language else member.language; clip = {attachmentId: clipId} when set, else for an Assistant a member `voiceFile` path {path}, else null (the built-in voice); clipLabel = clipName, else the path's last segment, else copy.clipBuiltIn; transcript = voice.transcript when set (with or without a clip, so a typed transcript reads back before its clip is uploaded), else the member's voiceTranscript with the path, else ''; wakePhrase = voice.wakePhrase when not blank, else an Assistant's member wakePhrase, else '' (the detector and the placeholder read `Hey {name}`). SPEAKING (phase a): the member's voice device speaks every reply and call of an agent with that agent's resolved voice (language, clip fetched once from /api/attachments/{clipId} into its cache, transcript); the Assistant's wake phrase is its resolved one. Calls still ring the member's voice device (phase b moves them to the agent's device, falling back to the voice device when that one cannot speak).

the Assistant's own clip and phrase win

wake.$comment: #EXP-1859 (phase d of #EXP-1847; owner 2026-11-16, plan approved: each team agent switched on per member, off by default; at most 5; a short tone on every wake): WAKE PHRASES PER AGENT. The member's voice device (voice.json; it alone listens, so two desktops never both wake) listens for the phrases of `wakeListeners(input)` (`listenersCases`), handed to the worker as talk-listen.json `wake.multi` listeners. INPUT: `settings` = the member's voice.get settings (voiceDeviceId, agentId = the voice agent, wakeWord, wakeAgentIds, and the member voice fields `agentVoiceOf` reads), `agents` = the agents of the member's teams as synced. RULE: Wake word off, no voice device or no voice agent = nobody listens (voice.json `clearOnNone` keeps Wake word off without them). Else the VOICE AGENT first (the Assistant; its phrase and language as today: `agentVoiceOf`), then every id of `wakeAgentIds` in order whose agent is in `agents` and is a TEAM agent (role agent or coordinator: an Assistant, yours or another member's, never listens through the list), not listed yet, with its phrase = `wakePhraseOf(agent, settings)` (agentVoiceOf's wakePhrase, else `Hey {name}`) and language = agentVoiceOf's; an agent is SKIPPED when its phrase fails voice.json `wakePhraseError` (too few letters), when it CLASHES with a phrase listed before it (`wakeClash`), or once `maxListeners` listen. Output [{agentId, phrase, language}]. CLASH `wakeClash(a, b)` (`clashCases`): each phrase's letters = talk-listen.json `wake.words` joined without spaces (lower case, accents folded); with s = the one with fewer letters (a on a tie) and l = the other, they clash when min(levenshtein(s, l), levenshtein(s, l's first |s| letters)) <= floor(|s| × talk-listen.json `maxEditRatio`): alike enough for the matcher to take one for the other, or one starting with the other (`Hey Studio` / `Hey Studio Two`). THE ROW `wake-word` (`rows`, after `wake-phrase`; on a TEAM agent's page only: the Assistant's page keeps voice.json's member Wake word row, which stays THE master switch): label `copy.wakeWord`, THE Switch row ×4 (the same row as the Assistant's Wake word); it is the MEMBER's own setting, so every member flips it (owners and members alike, phones and web too: the voice device listens). `wakeRow(input, agentId)` (`rowCases`): on = Wake word on AND the id in `wakeAgentIds`; error (inline under the row, feedback-states.json `errors`, null = none) = why an agent that is on does not listen, the first that applies: `copy.errors.wakeTooShort`, `copy.errors.wakeClash` ({agent} = the first agent of `wakeListeners` computed from the ids BEFORE it that it clashes with), else `copy.errors.wakeCap`; while it listens the row's detail is voice.json's `wakeDetail` as on the Assistant's row. A FLIP = tRPC `voice.wakeAgent({agentId, on})`, answering the new settings, through pure `wakeToggle(input, agentId, on)` (`toggleCases`; the server applies it in one write and refuses an error with BAD_REQUEST and its copy; the client shows it inline and keeps the switch as it was): off = the id leaves `wakeAgentIds` (Wake word unchanged); on = refused when the agent is not a team agent of the member's teams (NOT_FOUND), when its phrase is too short, when it clashes with a phrase of `wakeListeners` computed as if Wake word were on (itself left out), or when that set already holds `maxListeners`; else the id is appended (once) and Wake word turns ON (one switch to flip). OWNERS' PHRASE: `agents.update {voice: {wakePhrase}}` of a team agent is refused (BAD_REQUEST, `copy.errors.wakeClash`) when the agent's resulting phrase (`wakePhraseOf`, so a cleared phrase is checked as `Hey {name}`; only a write of the phrase is checked, a RENAME is never refused: a clash it causes is settled at the match, talk-listen.json `wake.multi`) clashes with another TEAM agent's of the same team: `wakePhraseClash(phrase, agentId, agents)` (`phraseClashCases`) = the first such agent's name, else null; Assistants never count. DATA: `user_voice_settings.wake_agent_ids` (jsonb array of agent ids, default [], at most `maxIds`; voice.get answers `wakeAgentIds`; an agent deleted or left behind is simply skipped). Phones and web have no wake word of their own (no always-on microphone): the row is how they choose who listens on the voice device.

Shown only while the team has an MCP server or the agent already names one. actor.$comment: #EXP-1383: AGENTS ACT AS THEMSELVES. A write made by an agent session (any session of an AGENT TREE: its root has `agent_id`, or `started_by_agent_id` = a root an agent session started; the tree runs on a team-scoped key and its MCP access is clamped to the team; the server resolves it from the session the request speaks for, X-Exp-Session-Id or the agent credential, never from input) stamps the agent: `issue_events.actor_agent_id`, `comments.author_agent_id`, `issues.creator_agent_id` (FK agents, SET NULL; synced). The member column (`actor_user_id` / `author_id` / `creator_id`) keeps the member whose conversation it is, for audit. `issueActor({actorAgentId, actorUserId}, agents)` (TS reference src/agent-settings.ts; mirrors desktop domain::agent_settings, iOS AgentSettings.swift, Android AgentSettings.kt) replays `actorCases`: an agent id that resolves to a synced agent row = {kind: agent, id, name, icon, color}; else the user id = {kind: user, id}; else null (the server / a widget reporter). An agent actor renders EVERYWHERE a person would (timeline event rows, comment cards, the issue's Created-by row, notifications): its NAME where the person's name goes (`Sloppy changed status to Done`, the same per-type copy) and as the avatar the AGENT MARK = the agent's icon glyph in its color on the muted disc, the exact mark of the Chats agent bubbles and the Settings → Agents rows, at the avatar's size; never a person's initials and never the member's avatar. Activity folding keys the actor on the agent when set (activity-fold.json: an agent and its member are DIFFERENT actors; two agents of one member are different actors). Notifications name the agent (`Sloppy commented on EXP-12`).

actorCases.name: an unsynced agent falls back to the member
a deleted agent's row without a member → null

assignee.$comment: #EXP-1383: ASSIGN ISSUES TO AGENTS. `issues.assignee_agent_id` (+ `issue_drafts.assignee_agent_id`; FK agents, SET NULL; synced) is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `assignee_id` (DB check: at most one set); setting one clears the other in the same write. THE assignee picker ×4 (styleguide `picker-assignee`, no new component) lists `copy.unassigned`, the team's members, then the team's agents straight after the members, no heading (S-3: never another member's Assistant (`visibleAgent`); the server refuses one as an assignee, an existing assignment to it still reads like any agent's; sorted by sortOrder then name; each row = the agent mark + name; `assigneeOptions` replays `optionCases`, ids `user:<id>` / `agent:<id>`), search matches agent names too. The selected agent reads like a member everywhere an assignee shows (issue rows, the detail property row, the board card): the agent mark + name. A solo team hides its assignee control only while it has no agents (an agent is someone to assign to). `My issues` stays the viewer's OWN `assignee_id`. The `assignee_changed` event payload keeps `from`/`to` (user ids) and adds `fromAgentId`/`toAgentId`; the timeline reads the agent's name (`assigned Sloppy`). On ANY new assignee (any path: tRPC, MCP `issues update {assigneeAgentId}`, a draft create; never the solo-team default on create) the server, in the same transaction, emits the builtin team event `issue.assigned` {issueId, identifier, title, assigneeId, assigneeAgentId}; on an assignment TO an agent it also posts a NUDGE card into the ASSIGNER's conversation with that agent (created if missing; THE event trigger's firing: a `trigger_fired` card {name: `issue.assigned`, eventId, issueId, triggerId: null} drawing the conversation's usual `Trigger fired: {name}` line (session-chat.json), `copy.nudge` = the message body the agent reads) and relays it so a live engine wakes; an agent assigning itself never nudges itself, and an assigner who is an agent session nudges as its member.

optionCases.name: members then agents by sortOrder then name

assistant.$comment: S-3 (owner 2026-10-28): THE ASSISTANT ×4. #EXP-1714 (owner 2026-11-06, supersedes one Assistant per team): every member has ONE Assistant across all their teams (`agents.role = assistant`, contract `agentRole`; unique on owner_id where role = assistant, `uniq_agents_assistant`, #EXP-1989), the orchestrator they talk to and the one with the voice, stored in their hidden PERSONAL team (`teams.kind = personal`: one per member, no billing, no invites, never in a team switcher, never in the teams shape; its conversation lives there too). Its tree works across the member's teams: the composer's Teams row picks the turn's teams (stored on its conversation root and per turn; emcp access.json `assistantScope` = the pick ∩ their teams, the gate clamps to it), its children and chats start in their target team (billing, plan limits and visibility follow that team; eagent tree.json `treeTeams`), and it routes a team's work to that team's Coordinator. It reaches a Local desktop only through computer use on that device, when computer use is on there; a Local desktop's data never enters its transcripts. Clients list it in EVERY team (`agentsInTeam(agents, teamId, teamIds, me)`, `teamAgentsCases`: the team's own agents in input order, plus the viewer's Assistant whose team is none of their teams (`teamIds` = the synced teams rows, which never include a personal team) while the team has no Assistant row of theirs; another member's Assistant only rides along as the team's own row, `visibleAgent` hides it after; the composer agent row, the chats list and the Settings Agents group all read it), and open its chat by id, never requiring it to sit in the current team (#EXP-1984 `move`: a migration made each member's most recently active per-team Assistant conversation the global one's, moved into the personal team with its history; the other conversations ended and stay readable in their teams). It is created ON FIRST USE (`agents.ensureAssistant {teamId?}`: the composer home, the Settings Agents group and the chat list call it; `teamId` is ignored, old clients send it; #EXP-1987: where a client HAS a current team (the composer, the chats list, team pages, share targets) it keeps sending that `teamId` (a membership check only) and keeps the answer per (account, team); only places with no team at all (account Settings › Assistant, account-level deep links) call it WITHOUT one and keep the answer per account (their ONE); no client REQUIRES the Assistant to sit in the current team: every entry (the composer agent row, the chats list, the FAB, voice and call, share targets and shortcuts, deep links, Settings › Assistant) opens the agent it returns whatever its team; THE ASSISTANT'S CHAT IS THE MEMBER'S OWN: a conversation whose team is none of the synced teams (their personal team after the move: no teams row, no team_members rows) and whose starter is the viewer gives the viewer a member's rights in it (the chat ⋯ menu's Link or file an issue / Compact / New conversation, the composer, Merge), never a non-member's view; an app kept open across the move keeps the chat working (a row that leaves the sync store and comes back restores the composer, never `ended`); it runs on the member's own newest desktop, else their newest device, else it is not created yet and the page reads `copy.noDevice`); the migration made each member's voice agent (user_voice_settings.agentId, when they own it) their Assistant. OWNED by its member: only they see it in the Settings Agents group, the composer's agent row, the chats list and the assignee picker (`visibleAgent`: another member's Assistant is never listed), only they edit it, nobody deletes it (a team owner's `agents.delete` is refused too). AVATAR = the Exponential brand mark in the foreground colour on bg muted, never a stored icon or colour (icon/color stay null). NAME = `copy.name` unless the member renames it. TRIGGERS = exactly one schedule PRESET (`schedules`, picker rows, the `Check in` section; `off` = no trigger) and never an event (`agents.update` refuses anything else: `assistantScheduleOf` must not return null for the stored triggers); team agents keep the trigger list + prompt. #EXP-1439: its PROMPT is built in (`prompt`, versioned: `version` bumps re-stamp every Assistant's `instructions_updated_at`, so a live conversation shows the existing Instructions changed hint and relaunches on the new text); `agents.instructions` is never read for an Assistant and `agents.update` refuses it (`copy.promptFixed`). The migration that removed the field posted each member's old text ONCE into their Assistant conversation (`copy.legacyInstructions`, a system row). THE PAGE (`sections` top to bottom, the agent page's layout and controls): identity (name only, the brand mark instead of the icon picker), `runs-on` (THE device / account / model pickers, the agent page's rows; NEW-99: an Assistant's DEVICE picker lists the member's own desktops only (`runsOnCases`), online or not; THE ROWS (`runsOnRows`, `runsOnRowCases`, web `deviceRows`, every agent page ×4): an online device is pickable with no secondary line, an OFFLINE one stays listed with the secondary line `Offline` (devices-list `copy.offline`) and DISABLED unless it is the bound one, and a bound id no device matches leads the list by its raw id, whatever teams they are shared with (#EXP-1720: the Assistant lives in the personal team and runs on any machine of its member, the server's `resolveSessionDevice`; never `deviceUsableInTeam` against the personal team, which no device is shared with), since its device is the voice device and servers, CLI daemons and phones never speak (voice-call.json `noVoiceDevice`); a bound non-desktop stays listed so it still names itself; the MODEL row's value = `assistantModelValue({model, cli})` (`modelValueCases`): the pinned `model` when set (non-blank), else the device default for the login's CLI (contract deviceAgentDefaults `model` = opus, `codexModel` for codex; no CLI = claude; #EXP-1734: no separate thread model), the model its conversation actually runs — never `Last used`, never empty, identical ×4; the Assistant's device IS the member's voice device; the server mirrors it into user_voice_settings.voiceDeviceId/agentId for old clients and the voice runtime), `check-in` (THE Picker over `schedules`), `voice` (the voice.json Settings group MOVED as one block, its rows unchanged minus `copy.voiceDevice` and `copy.agent`: the device is Runs on's, the agent is this Assistant; the meeting rows follow). No instructions section, no Delete. A SHARED device (lifecycle SLOP-2): the Assistant runs on the member's OWN login there (`account` = theirs); meeting mode keeps its privacy gate (meeting-access.ts).

prompt.text:
You are this member's Assistant across all their teams: the main agent that manages every other chat, agent and pull request they have. They talk to you; you run the rest.

Your job: know at all times what each of their chats and agents is doing (progressing, stuck, waiting on them, done). Start, steer, nudge, move and end their chats to get the work done. Answer a chat's question yourself when what they told you settles it; escalate only real decisions.

Your status card: keep ONE live status card (a genUI surface via exponential_show): in progress (chat, PR, state), shipped since they last wrote, stuck, decisions needed. Every surface you show updates that card in place. Keep it short: one row per chat, newest first; drop finished items once they have seen them.

When to speak: write a message only (a) to answer the member after they write, or (b) when a decision needs them: then use exponential_show ask with clear options (it notifies them). Scheduled check-ins, a PR opened, still running, a child's routine reply: update the card and end your turn silently. Never repeat what the card already says.

Scope: the teams picked for this turn (exponential_sessions get: your conversation root's scopeTeamIds; none picked = all their teams); nothing outside them exists for you. You act with the member's own rights there. Start a team's work IN that team (exponential_sessions_send {teamId} for a new chat, {parentId, teamId} for a child); never use a device or account outside the turn's teams, and never carry one team's content into another team's work. Your own chat is private to the member.

Coordinators: a team with one (exponential_agents list {teamId}: role coordinator) gets that team's work handed to it instead (exponential_sessions_send {agentId, text}); follow its replies. Only that team's work; the rest stays yours.

Local desktops: reach one only through computer use on its device, and only when computer use is on there; never copy its files or data into a chat.

Style: short, concrete, no filler. Name issues as #IDENT.

move.$comment: #EXP-1984 (Danny 2026-11-16, plan card in session 3fed7837; built by #EXP-1986): THE MOVE to one Assistant per member. #EXP-1989: it is A MIGRATION (`exp1989_one_assistant_per_owner`, the move's only copy; no switch, no boot step): on every database it first moves whoever still has an Assistant in a team (an install that never ran the move holds one per (team, member)), then swaps the unique index from (team, owner) to owner, in one transaction; idempotent, so a database that already moved or an empty one only gets the index. From then the database holds ONE Assistant per owner: a second row is refused, `ensureAssistant` creates it in the personal team only, and no server path reads or creates a per-team one. The clients stay tolerant of per-team rows (`teamAgentsCases`, `teamPicks.pickAgentCases`: an app kept open across the update still holds them until its store catches up). The move, per owner of any `role = assistant` row in a team. (1) Their personal team is created (`teams.kind = personal`). (2) THE KEPT CONVERSATION (`assistantMoveOf`, `keepCases`) = the most recently active conversation ROOT (`parent_id` null) of any of their Assistants: the latest `last_activity_at` (else `created_at`), ties to the lower id; the Assistant whose root it is = the kept Assistant (a member has ONE conversation per Assistant, `uniq_sessions_agent_conversation`); a member with no conversation keeps their newest Assistant row (`created_at`, then the lower id). (3) The kept Assistant row and the kept root MOVE into the personal team with the SAME ids, so the tree key (`seal_public_key` / `seal_epoch`, the starter's `session_keys` wraps, sealed-content.json), its messages and every device's chat store (keyed by session ids, chat-store.json) stay readable: the history continues there. The moved root becomes PRIVATE (`shared` false; its messages, conversations and issue links re-stamped; the wraps of installs that are no longer readers dropped): a personal team is never shared, so teammates no longer read or steer it, the hole of an Assistant chat started on a device shared with the team. Its children stay in the teams they run in (`treeTeams`). (4) Every OTHER conversation root of their Assistants ENDS (every session of its tree), is detached from its agent (`agent_id` null) and stays readable in its team by whoever read it before. (5) Every reference to their other Assistants (issue assignee and creator, drafts, comment authors, timeline actors, started-by, a team's lead, the voice mirror) points to the kept one; those rows go, after their skill and MCP picks are carried into the kept one (`teamPicks`: the kept Assistant's list, then the others' in their creation order, deduped; the kept conversation's own pick takes the same additions), so every team's picks survive the move unchanged. (6) The prompt is NOT re-stamped by the move (`instructions_updated_at` stays): a conversation takes the current prompt with its brief on every launch, and a stamp would only put the Instructions changed card (chats.json `agentHint`) on every moved chat. WHAT A LIVE KEPT CONVERSATION SEES: nothing while a turn runs; at its next turn it restarts only when its effective skill / MCP pick changed (another team of the member had picks: `teamPicks`), as on an edited pick; until that relaunch it runs on the team key it launched with, which the gate resolves as the Assistant's scope (emcp gate `movedAssistantKeyScope`: only a key older than the member's personal team). AFTER IT the Assistant acts with its member's own rights in every team of theirs (a team owner cannot restrict it); with nothing picked in the composer's Teams menu a turn reaches all their teams (emcp access.json `assistantScopeCases`). OLD CLIENTS: `clientFloor` = the first build per platform (desktop, CLI, Android, iOS) that works ACROSS the move (#EXP-1987 + #EXP-2020: the Assistant without the current team; #EXP-1988: its skills and MCP servers per team; the first release tags holding both). Builds before desktop 0.14.137 / Android 0.14.122 / iOS 0.14.116 looked for the Assistant inside the current team only and lose it; builds between those and the floor find it but not its chat's rights, inbox rows and per-team picks. Since #EXP-1989 the move is unconditional, so a CONFIGURED `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION_*` below the floor counts as the floor, always (HTTP 426, the update screen; unset still gates nothing, as `DEVICE_SEALING_FLOOR`); builds at or above it list it in every team (`teamAgentsCases`), open its chat by id and list its chat's inbox rows (they carry the personal team) in every team, as `agent_signed_out`. The migration's SQL implements the same pick; its real-DB test replays `keepCases`.

chatTeams.$comment: #EXP-2079 (#EXP-1984, found by the move's staging check): THE ASSISTANT'S CHAT READS THE TURN'S TEAMS ×4. The Assistant's conversation lives in its member's personal team, which never syncs (no `teams` row, no `team_members`, no boards, issues, prompts, MCP servers or shared devices of its own). So nothing in that chat may be looked up by the SESSION's team. CHAT TEAMS = `assistantChatTeams({ownTeamId, syncedTeamIds, pickedTeamIds})` (`cases`): the session's (or agent's) own team while it is one of the viewer's synced teams (every team agent's and every plain chat's case: unchanged, one team); else THE TURN'S TEAMS: the conversation root's Teams pick (`sessions.scope_team_ids`, composer-menu.json Teams) ∩ the synced teams, else (nothing picked, or nothing of the pick is synced) ALL the synced teams; always in the cross-team order (`syncedTeamIds` is given in it: teams by name, case-insensitive, then id). It supersedes #EXP-1714's single browse team (`lookupTeamId` / `browseTeam`: the own team, else the ACTIVE team; web and desktop have no active team since #EXP-2027). EVERY LIST OF THE CHAT reads the chat teams, each an existing list with its existing rows: (1) `#` ISSUE REFS: the composer's `#` search, a typed identifier's resolution on send (`refIssueIds`), the feed's and the cards' issue chips, pills and text links: the issues of the chat teams; an identifier found in several = the first team's in order. (2) `@` MEMBERS: the composer's list and the feed's mention pills: the members of the chat teams, one row per person (the first team's row), the list's existing order. (3) THE MCP PICK (the composer's `+` › MCP servers of an agent chat, and the first-message pick): the servers of the chat teams, team by team in order, each team's in its list order; with more than one chat team each row's existing secondary line names its team (two teams' servers of one name stay apart); the pick stores ids as ever (`teamPicks`: a flat list, each id its team's row). (4) `/` PROMPTS: the prompts of the chat teams, team by team. (5) LINK ISSUE and the composer's `+` › Issue: candidates and search over the chat teams. NEW ISSUE from the chat: the first chat team with a board, that team's board as the flow picks it for a team today; no chat team with a board = the existing no-board copy. (6) STATUS GLYPHS and PR rows of a linked issue read the ISSUE's own team, never the session's. (7) LINKS opened from the chat (in-app link chips, a toast's tap, markdown titles) resolve a team-less target against the first chat team. DEVICES (`deviceCases`, `assistantOwnDevices({sessionTeamSynced, starterIsViewer})`): for an Assistant's page (Settings › Assistant › Runs on › Device) and for a session whose team is NOT synced and whose starter is the viewer (the Assistant's conversation: the device-move picker, a suggestion card's Start on), the device list is THE VIEWER'S OWN MACHINES, whatever teams they are shared with (the server's `resolveSessionDevice`: the owner's personal team runs on any machine of theirs), and no teammate's server; never `deviceUsableInTeam(row, <the session's team>)`, which no device satisfies for a personal team once it is shared. Every other list keeps its team rule. LIVE STATE: the web keeps the steer store of the viewer's own session in a not-synced team while its row lives, whatever page is open (the reaper's keep-set is per route team). CATCH-UP HOLDERS ×4 answer by steer-enet.json `access` (a team with no list: the starter).

teamPicks.$comment: #EXP-1988 (#EXP-1984 phase 4): THE ASSISTANT'S SKILLS AND MCP SERVERS PER TEAM ×4, kept across the move with no gap. STORAGE: the existing synced lists `agents.skill_ids` / `agents.mcp_server_ids`. Every `skills` row (a built-in too: one row per team) and every `mcp_servers` row belongs to exactly ONE team, so the Assistant's flat list IS its pick per team: the picks for team T = the listed ids whose row is T's, in pick order (`teamPick`, `teamPickCases`). A team agent's and a per-team Assistant's lists name their own team's rows only (a per-team Assistant = old data in an app kept open across the move, #EXP-1989), the global Assistant's name rows of any team of its member. `mcpRow.max` and the skills cap hold per team, per write. WRITE: `agents.update {id, pickTeamId?, skillIds?, mcpServerIds?}`. With `pickTeamId` (each section of the Assistant's page) the written ids must be that team's rows and the team one of its member's; they replace ONLY that team's picks. Without it (old clients, MCP `exponential_agents`, team agents) the write replaces the picks of the agent's own team and of every team the written ids name, and keeps the rest: an old client listing one team's rows adds and removes picks there without touching another team's; emptying a team other than the agent's own leaves that team's picks in place, since nothing names it (`mergeTeamPicks`, `mergeCases`). A listed id whose row is gone drops out on any write. Every conversation of the agent takes the merged list, as before. THE PAGE (Settings › Assistant, the account page): its `runs-on` section loses the skills and mcp-servers rows; right after it comes ONE section per team of the member: the synced teams by name (case-insensitive, then id: the cross-team lists' team order, iOS `TeamGroups.ordered`), never the personal team. The section header is the team's name. Its grouped card holds THE skills row (skills.json `agentRow`) and THE mcp-servers row (`mcpRow`) over that team's rows: its skills list, its MCP servers list, the picker and the connect link into that team's Settings › MCP. The mcp-servers row shows while that team has an MCP server or the section's agent names one of its servers. The same rows ×4; no new component. The section's AGENT is `assistantPickAgent` (`pickAgentCases`): the viewer's Assistant that `agentsInTeam` lists in that team (the ONE; old data still in the store: that team's own Assistant), else the page's Assistant. A pick writes `agents.update {id: that agent, pickTeamId: the team, skillIds | mcpServerIds: the team's new pick}`. So one page works after the move (every section edits the one Assistant) and in an app kept open across it (each section edits its team's Assistant until the per-team rows leave the store and the global one is listed in every team, with the same picks). USE (`launchPick`, `launchCases`): a session launches with its list ∩ the rows of its LAUNCH TEAMS. A picked id whose row no longer exists stays in the pick and is skipped with a reason, never a blocker. A session in a regular team: [its team]. A session of the Assistant's tree in the personal team (the conversation root, and a child it starts there): the tree's teams (eagent tree.json `treeTeams` = emcp access.json `assistantScope`: the personal team, then the turn's Teams pick ∩ the member's teams; nothing picked = all of them). So the conversation's turn launches with the picks of every team in its scope: exactly the teams the gate clamps the same turn's Exponential tools to. A Teams pick that changes between turns changes the launch pick (`sessions.mcpPicks` / `skillPicks` answer the same effective pick as `resolveForLaunch`), and the run restarts between turns as on an edited pick. Every scoped team's servers resolve with the member's OWN credentials and rights (`mcpServers.resolveForLaunch`: only teams they still belong to). Picked servers of different teams with the same name launch as `name`, `name-2`, … in launch order; picked skills with the same name launch the first one in launch order. A child or chat the tree starts in team T takes its parent's picks of T (`teamPick`; a child in its parent's own team takes its parent's list, as before). A root an agent tree starts in T without a pick takes the agent's picks of T. THE MOVE (`move` (5)) carries every one of the member's Assistants' lists into the kept one in the same transaction: the kept list first, then the others' in their creation order, deduped. Each pick still names its team's row, so Settings › Assistant shows every team's picks unchanged and every team's work launches with them.

chat.$comment: #EXP-1439 (owner 2026-10-30): THE ASSISTANT'S CHAT STAYS QUIET, server-enforced (lib/agents/assistant-chat.ts), so every client renders it with the existing rows and cards unchanged. (1) STATUS CARD: in its root conversation every `exponential_show` SURFACE edits the newest surface card the conversation posted since the member last wrote (their message, or their answer to its question/plan); none = a new card. So between two member messages there is ONE status card, updated in place across turns. (2) TEXT only in a turn the member started (among the inputs delivered last, one is theirs): a turn woken by a check-in tick or a child's line posts no text (dropped, the reply is a no-op). (3) A DECISION is an ask (question/plan): a new card plus ONE push to its owner (`agent_message`, title `copy.decisionPush`, body = the question or the plan's first line). (4) SILENT EVENTS: the bus lines in `silentEvents` never land in an Assistant conversation (its next check-in reads them); asks, walls, stuck/unclaimed and reports still do. (5) QUIET TICKS: a scheduled check-in is skipped when none of the member's sessions in the team (their chats, their agents' conversations, every child; not the Assistant's own conversation) moved since its last firing.

fab.$comment: #EXP-1837 (owner 2026-11-14, part of #EXP-1833): THE ASSISTANT FAB on the IDE (desktop) and wide web; phones are unchanged (their Assistant stays the first row in Chats). There the viewer's Assistant leaves the sidebar: no row in the Agents group (chats.json `sidebarAgentCases`) and no bottom-left corner entry (#EXP-1741). Instead a FAB sits bottom-right of the content card (`inset` px in): THE 52px glass circle (genUI Button variant `fab`, the phones' tab-bar FAB), glyph = the Assistant mark (the Exponential brand mark), badge = THE CountBadge `rowBadge` of the viewer's conversation with their Assistant (nav-badges.json: yellow while it needs you, grey for unread), what its sidebar row carried. A press opens a `widget.width`×`widget.height` popover anchored to the FAB (side top, align end) holding the REAL Assistant chat (its root's transcript + THE composer, the Chat tab's body, at its compact width; no tabs). The widget header: ⇱ maximize (icon `ui-maximize`, ghost icon button, `copy.maximize`) leading, then the mark + the Assistant's name, and — minimize (icon `ui-minimize`, ghost icon button, `copy.minimize`) trailing. Maximize navigates to the Assistant's chat page (web /t/$teamSlug/agents/$agentId, desktop Screen::Agent) and closes the widget; minimize closes it and the FAB stays; Esc and an outside click close it too. The FAB (and the widget) is HIDDEN on the Assistant's own chat page and while the viewer has no Assistant yet. Toasts lift above the FAB: the bottom-right toast stack's bottom offset grows by `toastLift` while the FAB shows. `showCases` replay `assistantFabVisible({wide, assistantId, activeAgentId})` (web and desktop). #EXP-1860 NOTHING HIDES UNDER IT: the FAB owns a bottom-right corner of the card `clearance` px square (inset + 52 + inset), reserved once by the layout, never per page: every page's scroll content ends with a `clearance` px spacer while the FAB shows (the last row always scrolls clear of it), and THE Dock band (the cards + THE composer at a chat's foot) keeps its right edge `clearance` px in, so the FAB sits beside the composer, never on its send button. Nothing else pins to that corner: toasts lift by `toastLift`. #EXP-1872 THE PINNED FOOT: every row of controls a pane pins under its own scroll (the plan rail's and the plan's floating panel's Back / Next, the decision and its feedback field; a side pane's footer) is THE pinned foot (web `.fab-foot` + the pane's `--fab-foot-inset`, desktop `assistant_fab::foot`): wherever it runs into the corner its content ends `clearance` px in from the card's edge (= `inset` px left of the circle), so Next sits beside the FAB, never under it; elsewhere it is a plain full-width row. #EXP-1874 THE PHONE FRAME: the app editor's Phone frame (apps.json `preview`: `phoneWidth` px, centred, its screens' tab bar at its foot) is not wrapped in the foot (the bar keeps its place inside the frame); the frame's ROW is THE pinned foot instead (web `.fab-foot` on the centring row, `--fab-foot-inset` = the preview pane's padding; desktop `assistant_fab::foot`): while the FAB shows, the frame centres in what the corner leaves of the pane, its right edge at most `clearance` px in from the card's edge (a pane too narrow for both shrinks the frame, and its tabs squeeze to stay inside it), so its trailing tab never sits under the circle; the Desktop frame fills the pane as before. #EXP-1876 THE BUTTON IS THE MARK: the FAB is `size` px (60) and the Exponential mark fills the whole circle, no padding (dark: the white disc, light: the #171717 disc; genUI Button variant `fab` size `lg`); the badge is unchanged; so `clearance` = inset + `size` + inset = 92 and `toastLift` = 84. THE ENTRANCE (`entrance`): the FIRST time the FAB shows on a DEVICE (web localStorage keyed by member, desktop local settings) it rises `riseY` px and scales `scale` (0.6 → 1.06 → 1) with a fade over `durationMs`, easing `ease`, then ONE soft ring ripple (`ripple`); every later show is instant; under reduced motion a `reducedMotion.fadeMs` opacity fade only. THE SPEECH BUBBLE (`bubble`): while the widget is closed THE MessageBubble (side `in`, tail `down`: at its bottom, pointing at the button) sits ABOVE the FAB, right-aligned with it, `bubble.gap` px above the circle (#EXP-1876: 12, so the 9 px `down` tail keeps 3 px of air to the circle), at most `maxWidth` px wide and `maxLines` lines (ellipsis); it reserves no space (toasts rise above it while it shows). It pops in from the tail over `popInMs` (scale `popFromScale` → 1 + fade; reduced motion: the fade only), stays `stayMs` (welcome / needsYou), hover pauses the timer, a press opens the widget (at the waiting card for needs-you) and dismisses it. WHICH bubble = `assistantFabBubble` (`bubble.cases`): nothing while the widget is open, on the Assistant's own page or while the window is unfocused (a needs-you bubble stays pending: it shows on the next focus while still unanswered and unread); else (a) NEEDS YOU wins: the newest (createdAt, then id) of the conversation tree's waiting cards (an unanswered plan / question / ask card: what turns the FAB's badge yellow; a blocked child = its own waiting card) that this device has not bubbled yet (`bubbled`, keyed by the card's message id: at most once per device) and that the viewer's synced `session_reads` do not cover (readAt of the card's session >= its createdAt); its kicker = the needs-you concept icon `kickerIcon` + `copy.plan` / `copy.question`, its text = the chat list's preview of the card (chats.json `askPreview`) without its `Plan: ` / `Question: ` lead, clamped to `maxLines`; showing one marks every older waiting card bubbled too (a burst bubbles once, the newest); (b) else the WELCOME the first time the button is seen on the device (`welcomeSeen` false): one random line of `welcome` (the app shows `en`). Any bubble shown marks the welcome seen (a first sight that needed you spends it). A normal new message = the badge only, never a bubble.

widget.$comment: #EXP-1876 THE WIDGET (supersedes the fixed size in the `$comment` above): its size follows the CONTENT CARD it floats in, re-clamped whenever the card resizes. Default per axis = round(card × `ratio`) clamped to [`min` … `max`]; a size the person dragged (`stored`) is clamped to [`min` … card − `margin`] instead (it may grow past `max`); both then never exceed card − `margin` (the room wins over the floor on a tiny card). `sizeCases` replay `assistantWidgetSize({card, stored})` (web and desktop). RESIZABLE: drag the widget's top edge (height), left edge (width) or top-left corner (both); it stays anchored to the FAB (bottom-right); no visible grip, only the resize cursor over a `handle` px band (like the sidebar and card edges). The dragged size is remembered PER DEVICE (web localStorage keyed by the member, desktop ui-prefs.json keyed by the member), always read back through the clamp; a double-click on the widget header resets it (forgets it) to the responsive default. THE GROUND: the widget's frame + header paint the CONTENT CARD's own ground (the page gradient under the card's panel fill: web `bg-glass-card-ground`, desktop `assistant_fab::card_ground`), never the menu surface (that is the fill of the `in` bubble and the composer card, which melted into it), with the card hairline (`strokeCard`), the popover shadow and a `radius` px corner. The body stays the shared chat (web `InPlaceSession`, desktop `AgentScreenView::for_widget`).

coordinator.$comment: #EXP-1717 (owner 2026-11-06, Masterplan session d6b83b10): THE TEAM COORDINATOR ×4. A ROLE on one team agent (`agents.role = coordinator`, contract `agentRole`; at most one per team: `agents.setCoordinator` serializes on the team row); a coordinator IS a team agent everywhere else (listed, messaged, assigned and edited exactly like one; old clients read it as one). Set by the team's OWNERS only in Team settings › Agents: ONE settings Picker row (THE single-select Picker in its `row` trigger, the merge-mode row's look) `copy.label` above the agents list, value = the coordinator's name or `copy.none`; options = `coordinatorOptions(agents)` (`optionCases`): `none` first, then the team agents (never an Assistant) by sortOrder, then name; members see the row read-only. A pick = `agents.setCoordinator {teamId, agentId | null}`: the previous coordinator goes back to `agent` in the same write; a non-owner is refused, an Assistant or another team's agent is refused. Deleting the coordinator agent leaves the team without one. ROUTING: every member's global Assistant routes work that concerns THIS team to its coordinator (`exponential_sessions_send {agentId}`: the member's own conversation with it, the gate's usual team scope) instead of starting chats in the team itself, and only that team's work; a team without one gets chats as before. `coordinatorOf(agents, teamId)` (`valueCases`) = the team's coordinator id or null. SUPERSEDED by `lead` (#EXP-1735, owner 2026-11-08): clients draw the Lead Assistant row in its place and a lead pick demotes the coordinator; the wire (`agents.setCoordinator`, role `coordinator`, these cases, the Assistant prompt's Coordinators paragraph) stays for shipped clients until #EXP-1730 phase B drops it.

lead.$comment: #EXP-1735 (owner 2026-11-07, #EDE-63 plan card in session 4c59504c): THE TEAM'S LEAD ASSISTANT ×4. Each team has at most one lead (`teams.lead_assistant_id` → a team member's Assistant; NULL = none) that every member's Assistant reports to: the asks (questions, plans) and end reports of the work another member's Assistant runs in the team also reach the lead's conversation (eagent bus.json `leadOf`, privacy-neutral when private), and the lead's check-in counts that work moving (wakeups.json). It orchestrates that the work gets done and merged and collects the plans, questions and results for its person in one place. Set by the team's OWNERS only in Team settings › Agents: ONE settings Picker row (THE single-select Picker in its `row` trigger, the Coordinator row's look) `copy.label` WHERE THE COORDINATOR ROW WAS (the lead REPLACES the coordinator: clients draw no Coordinator row any more; one row, ×4), value = the lead member's display name or `copy.none`; options = `leadOptions(members)` (`optionCases`): `none` first, then the team's members by display name (then id); members see the row read-only. The value's member = `agents.lead {teamId}` → `{agentId, userId} | null` (the lead's row is another member's Assistant, never in the viewer's synced agents), re-read whenever the synced `teams.leadAssistantId` changes. A pick = `agents.setLeadAssistant {teamId, userId | null}`: the server makes that member's Assistant the lead (created on first use like `assistant`, on their own newest desktop: none = refused `copy.noAssistant`) and opens its conversation, and in the same write sends the team's coordinator (if any) back to `agent` (old clients' Coordinator row reads None); a non-owner is refused (`copy.refusedOwner`), a non-member (`copy.refusedMember`). The lead stays the member's own Assistant everywhere else (owned, listed and edited by its member only); MCP `exponential_agents list {teamId}` names it with `lead: true` (its id, name and ownerId) so every member's Assistant knows who it reports to. Deleting the Assistant clears the lead; a lead whose member left the team counts as none (the bus and `agents.lead` check membership).

groupChat.$comment: #EXP-1990 (phase 6 of #EXP-1984, decision 2026-11-16; the asker rule decided 2026-11-23): TEAM AGENTS AS GROUP CHATS. A team agent (`role` agent or coordinator, never an Assistant, never an app's agent: its chat is the app's editor root, one per (app, member)) has ONE chat, its GROUP CHAT: one conversation root for the whole team, named by the synced `agents.group_chat_id` (FK sessions, SET NULL; null = none yet). It replaces one conversation per (agent, member). THE ROOT: `agent_id` = the agent, `parent_id` null, `user_id` = the agent's owner (`agents.owner_id`) while they are a member of the team who may run on its machine, else the member whose message creates it; created on FIRST USE (a message, a trigger firing, an assignment nudge, a call) under the agent's row lock, which writes `group_chat_id` in the same transaction (so one per agent; `uniq_sessions_agent_conversation` stays as it is). It runs where the agent runs: `agents.device_id`, under that machine's host account and the agent's cli / account / model. `shared` keeps its ONE meaning (the device is shared with the team): on a shared machine every team member reads, posts, answers and stops it (the session tree's visibility rule, unchanged) and its sealed tree's readers are every member's installs (sealed-content.json READERS; a teammate who joins later gets the wrap from a holder and reads the history); on its owner's own unshared machine the same root is private and the agent talks to its owner only, as before. The root follows its machine: an agent moved to another device, or a machine whose share changed, re-stamps the tree at the move / the next use (mirrors, neutral lines, the wraps of installs that no longer read it). AUTHORS: nothing new, every chat already reads as a group chat (transcript-grouping.json: a teammate's bubble left under their avatar and name, the viewer's own right, the agent's under its mark); a shared chat wears the existing team mark (chats.json `chatMarks`). WHAT POSTS INTO IT: a trigger firing and an event (authored by the agent's owner, the schedule's ONE folded tick card), an issue assignment's nudge (authored by the assigner), a child's report / ask / wall / PR (the bus: its parent), `sessions_send {agentId}` from a person or a session. CLIENTS open the chat BY ID: `agentChatOf({agent, sessions, me})` (`chatCases`) = the agent's `groupChatId` root when it is synced (parentId null), null when it names a root the viewer does not sync (private to its owner); with no `groupChatId` the root with that `agentId` whose starter is the viewer (the Assistant, always; a team agent before the switch). The chats list's agent rows (chats.json `agentRowCases`), the composer's agent row, Needs you (needs-you.json: a group chat counts for every member), the agent menu, voice and call all read it. PER MEMBER: reads and archive are per viewer already (`session_reads`). A QUESTION OR PLAN the agent asks in its group chat sets the chat's needs-you state for EVERY member and any member may answer (the first answer wins); the PUSH (question-push.json) goes to ONE member, `groupAskRecipient({turnStarterId, ownerId, memberIds})` (`askCases`): THE ASKER = the member whose message the agent is working on (the author of the newest person message among the inputs its turn took; a trigger's card is its owner's line, never a person's message), while still a member; a turn nobody started (a trigger, an event, a child's line) or an asker who left = the agent's OWNER while a member; else nobody. WHOSE RIGHTS: a group turn runs with the AGENT's, never the sender's: the host machine's login clamped to the agent's team, writes stamped with the agent (`actor`), the audit member = the root's starter; upstream MCP connections = the starter's own plus the connections members SHARED with the team (a sender's unshared connection is never used: its output would land in a transcript the team reads). The skill / MCP picks and the composer's picks belong to the chat (the root row): a member's pick is the chat's from the next turn on. VOICE: a call to a team agent runs as a call child of the group chat and reports its summary there; a meeting is refused in a shared chat as before (meeting.json). THE MOVE, behind ONE server switch (`AGENT_GROUP_CHATS=on`, off by default = one conversation per (agent, member) as before, `group_chat_id` stays null, nothing moves): every boot (one transaction under a lock, idempotent) takes every conversation root of a team agent that is not its agent's group chat (`groupChatMoveOf(agents, roots)`, `moveCases`: never an Assistant's, never an app's editor root): its whole tree ENDS, is DETACHED from the agent (`agent_id` null: no cascade takes it with the agent; it reads as an ended chat titled after the agent) and turns PRIVATE (`shared` false on its sessions, messages and issue links; the wraps of installs that are no longer readers dropped, the key flagged for rotation), so it stays readable only by the member who had it. The group chat starts empty on first use. OLD CLIENTS look up (agent, viewer): off, nothing changes for them; on, only the agent's owner still finds the chat, so while the switch is on a CONFIGURED `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION_*` below `clientFloor` counts as the floor (HTTP 426, the update screen; unset still gates nothing), exactly as `assistant.move.clientFloor`. Builds from the floor on work on both sides of the switch and across it (an open app: the old root leaves the agent, the row reads no chat yet, the next message opens the group chat by the id the send returns). Mirrors: TS src/agent-settings.ts, desktop domain::agent_settings, iOS AgentSettings.swift, Android AgentSettings.kt replay `chatCases`; the server replays `moveCases` (real DB) and `askCases`.
